newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican oil spill soils river in Veracruz.
newsitem.headline: Mexican oil spill soils river in Veracruz.

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil monopoly Pemex spilled a 260-gallon (1,000-liter) mixture of oil and water into a river near the Gulf of Mexico coast on Monday, Pemex said on Wedneday.
The company offered no explanation about why it reported the spill two days after it occurred.

Environmental groups that had been denouncing the spill at the San Andres II plant for two days claimed it was far worse than Pemex admitted, saying that up to 26 miles (42 km) of the Tecolutla River were soiled.

Pemex clean-up teams "contained the flow of water mixed with oil, which was estimated to be about 50 liters (13 galllons) of hydrocarbons dissolved in approximately 1,000 liters (260 gallons) of water," Pemex said in a statement.
Pemex said "at no time was there environmental damage nor any danger to the population."
But two Mexican environmental groups disputed Pemex's version.

The Regional Ecological Council of Veracruz state said the spill left a foul odor and large amounts of oil "that are running toward the delta, estuaries and tourist beaches of Tecolutla and Costa Esmeralda."
The coastline in question is in northern Veracruz state, about 120 miles (200 km) east of Mexico City.

The Group of 100, Mexico's leading environmental watchdog group, said in a statement that 15 to 18 miles (24 to 30 km) of the river was affected by the spill. The group said the river was rich in fish and freshwater crabs, oysters and shrimp.
"The inexplicable is how a spill of this magnitude can happen in Mexico and for days Pemex doesn't report it and the government does nothing," the Group of 100 said.
